3	const { LruMap: Lru } = require('toad-cache')
4	
5	/**
6	 * keyValuePairsReg is used to split the parameters list into associated
7	 * key value pairings. The leading `(?:^|;)\s*` anchor ensures the regex
8	 * only attempts matches at parameter boundaries, preventing quadratic
9	 * backtracking on malformed input.
10	 *
11	 * @see https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc9110.html#parameter
12	 * @type {RegExp}
13	 */
14	const keyValuePairsReg = /(?:^|;)\s*([\w!#$%&'*+.^`|~-]+)=([^;]*)/gm
15	
16	/**
17	 * typeNameReg is used to validate that the first part of the media-type
18	 * does not use disallowed characters. Types must consist solely of
19	 * characters that match the specified character class. It must terminate
20	 * with a matching character.
21	 *
22	 * @see https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc9110.html#rule.token.separators
23	 * @type {RegExp}
24	 */
25	const typeNameReg = /^[\w!#$%&'*+.^`|~-]+$/
26	
27	/**
28	 * subtypeNameReg is used to validate that the second part of the media-type
29	 * does not use disallowed characters. Subtypes must consist solely of
30	 * characters that match the specified character class, and optionally
31	 * terminated with any amount of whitespace characters. Without the terminating
32	 * anchor (`$`), the regular expression will match the leading portion of a
33	 * string instead of the whole string.
34	 *
35	 * @see https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc9110.html#rule.token.separators
36	 * @type {RegExp}
37	 */
38	const subtypeNameReg = /^[\w!#$%&'*+.^`|~-]+\s*$/
39	
40	/**
41	 * Content-Type internal shared cache
42	 * @type {Lru<ContentType>}
43	 */
44	const cache = new Lru(100)
45	
46	/**
47	 * ContentType parses and represents the value of the content-type header.
48	 *
49	 * @see https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc9110.html#media.type
50	 * @see https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc9110.html#parameter
51	 */
52	class ContentType {
53	  #valid = false
54	  #empty = true
55	  #type = ''
56	  #subtype = ''
57	  #parameters = new Map()
58	  #string
59	
60	  /**
61	   * The shared cache of ContentType instances. The cache is used to avoid
62	   * creating multiple instances of ContentType for the same header value.
63	   * @type {Lru<ContentType>}
64	   */
65	  static get cache () { return cache }
66	
67	  /**
68	   * Create a ContentType instance from a header value. If the value has been
69	   * previously parsed, the cached instance will be returned.
70	   * @param {string} headerValue
71	   * @returns {ContentType | undefined}
72	   */
73	  static from (headerValue) {
74	    let contentType = cache.get(headerValue)
75	    if (contentType !== undefined) return contentType
76	    contentType = new ContentType(headerValue)
77	    cache.set(headerValue, contentType)
78	    return contentType
79	  }
80	
81	  constructor (headerValue) {
82	    if (headerValue == null || headerValue === '' || headerValue === 'undefined') {
83	      return
84	    }
85	
86	    let sepIdx = headerValue.indexOf(';')
87	    if (sepIdx === -1) {
88	      // The value is the simplest `type/subtype` variant.
89	      sepIdx = headerValue.indexOf('/')
90	      if (sepIdx === -1) {
91	        // Got a string without the correct `type/subtype` format.
92	        return
93	      }
94	
95	      const type = headerValue.slice(0, sepIdx).trimStart().toLowerCase()
96	      const subtype = headerValue.slice(sepIdx + 1).trimEnd().toLowerCase()
97	
98	      if (
99	        typeNameReg.test(type) === true &&
100	        subtypeNameReg.test(subtype) === true
101	      ) {
102	        this.#valid = true
103	        this.#empty = false
104	        this.#type = type
105	        this.#subtype = subtype
106	      }
107	
108	      return
109	    }
110	
111	    // We have a `type/subtype; params=list...` header value.
112	    const mediaType = headerValue.slice(0, sepIdx).toLowerCase()
113	    const paramsList = headerValue.slice(sepIdx + 1).trim()
114	
115	    sepIdx = mediaType.indexOf('/')
116	    if (sepIdx === -1) {
117	      // We got an invalid string like `something; params=list...`.
118	      return
119	    }
120	    const type = mediaType.slice(0, sepIdx).trimStart()
121	    const subtype = mediaType.slice(sepIdx + 1).trimEnd()
122	
123	    if (
124	      typeNameReg.test(type) === false ||
125	      subtypeNameReg.test(subtype) === false
126	    ) {
127	      // Some portion of the media-type is using invalid characters. Therefore,
128	      // the content-type header is invalid.
129	      return
130	    }
131	    this.#type = type
132	    this.#subtype = subtype
133	    this.#valid = true
134	    this.#empty = false
135	
136	    let matches = keyValuePairsReg.exec(paramsList)
137	    while (matches) {
138	      // https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc9110.html#parameter
139	      // Parameter names are case-insensitive.
140	      const key = matches[1].toLowerCase()
141	      // Parameter values might or might not be case-sensitive,
142	      // depending on the semantics of the parameter name.
143	      const value = matches[2]
144	      if (value[0] === '"') {
145	        if (value.at(-1) !== '"') {
146	          this.#parameters.set(key, 'invalid quoted string')
147	          matches = keyValuePairsReg.exec(paramsList)
148	          continue
149	        }
150	        // We should probably verify the value matches a quoted string
151	        // (https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc9110.html#rule.quoted-string) value.
152	        // But we are not really doing much with the parameter values, so we
153	        // are omitting that at this time.
154	        this.#parameters.set(key, value.slice(1, value.length - 1))
155	      } else {
156	        this.#parameters.set(key, value)
157	      }
158	      matches = keyValuePairsReg.exec(paramsList)
159	    }
160	  }
161	
162	  get [Symbol.toStringTag] () { return 'ContentType' }
163	
164	  get isEmpty () { return this.#empty }
165	
166	  get isValid () { return this.#valid }
167	
168	  get mediaType () { return `${this.#type}/${this.#subtype}` }
169	
170	  get type () { return this.#type }
171	
172	  get subtype () { return this.#subtype }
173	
174	  get parameters () { return this.#parameters }
175	
176	  toString () {
177	    /* c8 ignore next: we don't need to verify the cache */
178	    if (this.#string) return this.#string
179	    const parameters = []
180	    for (const [key, value] of this.#parameters.entries()) {
181	      parameters.push(`${key}="${value}"`)
182	    }
183	    const result = [this.#type, '/', this.#subtype]
184	    if (parameters.length > 0) {
185	      result.push('; ')
186	      result.push(parameters.join('; '))
187	    }
188	    this.#string = result.join('')
189	    return this.#string
190	  }
191	}
192	
193	module.exports = ContentType

3	const { describe, test } = require('node:test')
4	const ContentType = require('../lib/content-type')
5	const Fastify = require('..')
6	
7	test('should remove content-type for setErrorHandler', async t => {
8	  t.plan(8)
9	  let count = 0
10	
11	  const fastify = Fastify()
12	  fastify.setErrorHandler(function (error, request, reply) {
13	    t.assert.strictEqual(error.message, 'kaboom')
14	    t.assert.strictEqual(reply.hasHeader('content-type'), false)
15	    reply.code(400).send({ foo: 'bar' })
16	  })
17	  fastify.addHook('onSend', async function (request, reply, payload) {
18	    count++
19	    t.assert.strictEqual(typeof payload, 'string')
20	    switch (count) {
21	      case 1: {
22	        // should guess the correct content-type based on payload
23	        t.assert.strictEqual(reply.getHeader('content-type'), 'text/plain; charset=utf-8')
24	        throw Error('kaboom')
25	      }
26	      case 2: {
27	        // should guess the correct content-type based on payload
28	        t.assert.strictEqual(reply.getHeader('content-type'), 'application/json; charset=utf-8')
29	        return payload
30	      }
31	      default: {
32	        t.fail('should not reach')
33	      }
34	    }
35	  })
36	  fastify.get('/', function (request, reply) {
37	    reply.send('plain-text')
38	  })
39	
40	  const { statusCode, body } = await fastify.inject({ method: 'GET', path: '/' })
41	  t.assert.strictEqual(statusCode, 400)
42	  t.assert.strictEqual(body, JSON.stringify({ foo: 'bar' }))
43	})

45	describe('ContentType class', () => {
46	  test('returns empty instance for empty value', (t) => {
47	    let found = new ContentType('')
48	    t.assert.equal(found.isEmpty, true)
49	
50	    found = new ContentType('undefined')
51	    t.assert.equal(found.isEmpty, true)
52	
53	    found = new ContentType()
54	    t.assert.equal(found.isEmpty, true)
55	  })
56	
57	  test('indicates media type is not correct format', (t) => {
58	    let found = new ContentType('foo')
59	    t.assert.equal(found.isEmpty, true)
60	    t.assert.equal(found.isValid, false)
61	
62	    found = new ContentType('foo /bar')
63	    t.assert.equal(found.isEmpty, true)
64	    t.assert.equal(found.isValid, false)
65	
66	    found = new ContentType('foo/ bar')
67	    t.assert.equal(found.isEmpty, true)
68	    t.assert.equal(found.isValid, false)
69	
70	    found = new ContentType('foo; param=1')
71	    t.assert.equal(found.isEmpty, true)
72	    t.assert.equal(found.isValid, false)
73	
74	    found = new ContentType('foo/π; param=1')
75	    t.assert.equal(found.isEmpty, true)
76	    t.assert.equal(found.isValid, false)
77	
78	    found = new ContentType('application/json<script>alert(1)</script>')
79	    t.assert.equal(found.isEmpty, true)
80	    t.assert.equal(found.isValid, false)
81	
82	    found = new ContentType('application/json/extra/slashes')
83	    t.assert.equal(found.isEmpty, true)
84	    t.assert.equal(found.isValid, false)
85	
86	    found = new ContentType('application/json(garbage)')
87	    t.assert.equal(found.isEmpty, true)
88	    t.assert.equal(found.isValid, false)
89	
90	    found = new ContentType('application/json@evil')
91	    t.assert.equal(found.isEmpty, true)
92	    t.assert.equal(found.isValid, false)
93	
94	    found = new ContentType('application/json\x00garbage')
95	    t.assert.equal(found.isEmpty, true)
96	    t.assert.equal(found.isValid, false)
97	  })
98	
99	  test('subtype with multiple fields validates as incorrect', (t) => {
100	    let found = new ContentType('application/json whatever')
101	    t.assert.equal(found.isValid, false)
102	    t.assert.equal(found.isEmpty, true)
103	
104	    found = new ContentType('application/    json whatever')
105	    t.assert.equal(found.isValid, false)
106	    t.assert.equal(found.isEmpty, true)
107	
108	    found = new ContentType('application/json whatever; foo=bar')
109	    t.assert.equal(found.isValid, false)
110	    t.assert.equal(found.isEmpty, true)
111	
112	    found = new ContentType('application/    json whatever; foo=bar')
113	    t.assert.equal(found.isValid, false)
114	    t.assert.equal(found.isEmpty, true)
115	  })
116	
117	  test('returns a plain media type instance', (t) => {
118	    const found = new ContentType('Application/JSON')
119	    t.assert.equal(found.mediaType, 'application/json')
120	    t.assert.equal(found.type, 'application')
121	    t.assert.equal(found.subtype, 'json')
122	    t.assert.equal(found.parameters.size, 0)
123	  })
124	
125	  test('handles empty parameters list', (t) => {
126	    const found = new ContentType('Application/JSON ;')
127	    t.assert.equal(found.isEmpty, false)
128	    t.assert.equal(found.mediaType, 'application/json')
129	    t.assert.equal(found.type, 'application')
130	    t.assert.equal(found.subtype, 'json')
131	    t.assert.equal(found.parameters.size, 0)
132	  })
133	
134	  test('returns a media type instance with parameters', (t) => {
135	    const found = new ContentType('Application/JSON ; charset=utf-8; foo=BaR;baz=" 42"')
136	    t.assert.equal(found.isEmpty, false)
137	    t.assert.equal(found.mediaType, 'application/json')
138	    t.assert.equal(found.type, 'application')
139	    t.assert.equal(found.subtype, 'json')
140	    t.assert.equal(found.parameters.size, 3)
141	
142	    const expected = [
143	      ['charset', 'utf-8'],
144	      ['foo', 'BaR'],
145	      ['baz', ' 42']
146	    ]
147	    t.assert.deepStrictEqual(
148	      Array.from(found.parameters.entries()),
149	      expected
150	    )
151	
152	    t.assert.equal(
153	      found.toString(),
154	      'application/json; charset="utf-8"; foo="BaR"; baz=" 42"'
155	    )
156	  })
157	
158	  test('skips invalid quoted string parameters', (t) => {
159	    const found = new ContentType('Application/JSON ; charset=utf-8; foo=BaR;baz=" 42')
160	    t.assert.equal(found.isEmpty, false)
161	    t.assert.equal(found.mediaType, 'application/json')
162	    t.assert.equal(found.type, 'application')
163	    t.assert.equal(found.subtype, 'json')
164	    t.assert.equal(found.parameters.size, 3)
165	
166	    const expected = [
167	      ['charset', 'utf-8'],
168	      ['foo', 'BaR'],
169	      ['baz', 'invalid quoted string']
170	    ]
171	    t.assert.deepStrictEqual(
172	      Array.from(found.parameters.entries()),
173	      expected
174	    )
175	
176	    t.assert.equal(
177	      found.toString(),
178	      'application/json; charset="utf-8"; foo="BaR"; baz="invalid quoted string"'
179	    )
180	  })
181	})
182	
183	describe('ContentType class cache', () => {
184	  test('allow access cache', (t) => {
185	    const contentType1 = ContentType.from('application/json')
186	    const contentType2 = ContentType.cache.get('application/json')
187	    t.assert.equal(contentType1, contentType2)
188	  })
189	
190	  test('returns same instance for the same content type string', (t) => {
191	    const contentType1 = ContentType.from('application/json')
192	    const contentType2 = ContentType.from('application/json')
193	    t.assert.equal(contentType1, contentType2)
194	  })
195	
196	  test('returns different instances for different content type strings', (t) => {
197	    const contentType1 = ContentType.from('application/json')
198	    const contentType2 = ContentType.from('text/plain')
199	    t.assert.notEqual(contentType1, contentType2)
200	  })
201	})

 * only attempts matches at parameter boundaries, preventing quadratic

/**
 * keyValuePairsReg is used to split the parameters list into associated
 * key value pairings. The leading `(?:^|;)\s*` anchor ensures the regex
 * only attempts matches at parameter boundaries, preventing quadratic
 * backtracking on malformed input.
 *
 * A parameter value is either a token or a quoted-string. The quoted-string
 * alternative matches the whole quoted value, including any `;` characters
 * within it, so that such characters are not mistaken for a parameter
 * separator. The two alternatives of the value, and the two alternatives of
 * the quoted-string content, can never match the same character, so the
 * regex cannot backtrack.
 *
 * @see https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc9110.html#parameter
 * @see https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc9110.html#rule.quoted-string
 * @type {RegExp}
 */
const keyValuePairsReg = /(?:^|;)\s*([\w!#$%&'*+.^`|~-]+)=([\w!#$%&'*+.^`|~-]+|"(?:[\t \x21\x23-\x5b\x5d-\x7e\x80-\xff]|\\[\t \x21-\x7e\x80-\xff])*")/gm

/**
 * quotedPairReg is used to unescape the quoted-pairs found in the content of
 * a quoted-string.
 *
 * @see https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc9110.html#quoted.string
 * @type {RegExp}
 */
const quotedPairReg = /\\([\t \x21-\x7e\x80-\xff])/g

content.text:
Fixed. Changes:

**`lib/content-type.js:22`** — the parameter value alternative is now `token / quoted-string` per [RFC 9110 §5.6.6](https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc9110.html#parameter), with the quoted-string content following the qdtext (`\t`, SP, `!`, `\x23-\x5b`, `\x5d-\x7e`, obs-text) and quoted-pair (`\` + HTAB/SP/VCHAR/obs-text) ranges, instead of the `;`-unaware `[^;]*`. Added `quotedPairReg` (`lib/content-type.js:31`) and, in the constructor (`lib/content-type.js:155-168`), the enclosing DQUOTEs are stripped and quoted-pairs unescaped. The `'invalid quoted string'` sentinel is gone: an unterminated quoted value no longer matches the regex at all, so the parameter is dropped. The two value alternatives (and the two inside the quoted-string) are disjoint on their first character, so the added alternation can't backtrack.

Verified against the old parser that all three cases were broken on `main` and are fixed now:

| input | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `name="foo;bar"` | `name` → `invalid quoted string` | `name` → `foo;bar` |
| `name="a=b;charset=fake"` | `name` → sentinel, **plus phantom `charset` → `fake"`** | `name` → `a=b;charset=fake` only |
| `name="a\"b\\c"` | `a\"b\\c` | `a"b\c` |

**Tests** — `test/content-type.test.js`: three new unit tests for the above, and `skips invalid quoted string parameters` now expects the unterminated `baz=" 42` to be dropped (2 params, no sentinel in `toString()`). `test/internals/reply.test.js:1273`: integration test that `reply.send()` still appends `charset=utf-8` for `application/json; profile="a=b;charset=fake"` — that phantom `charset` previously satisfied `parameters.has('charset')` in `lib/reply.js:216` and suppressed the default.

Both touched test files pass (`content-type.test.js`: 14/14, `internals/reply.test.js`: 82/82). I could not run eslint — the command needed approval.

One consequence of the stricter grammar worth flagging: an *unquoted* value that isn't a valid token, e.g. `boundary=--abc=def`, now parses as `--abc` (the token prefix) rather than the whole string. Such values are required to be quoted by the RFC, and `fast-content-type-parse` rejects them outright; the only place fastify re-emits parameters is the JSON-charset branch of `reply.send()`, so this is unreachable for the `multipart` case where non-token boundaries actually occur.

One consequence of the stricter grammar worth flagging: an *unquoted* value that isn't a valid token, e.g. `boundary=--abc=def`, now parses as `--abc` (the token prefix) rather than the whole string. Such values are required to be quoted by the RFC, and `fast-content-type-parse` rejects them outright; the only place fastify re-emits parameters is the JSON-charset branch of `reply.send()`, so this is unreachable for the `multipart` case where non-token boundaries actually occur.
